 Hands-on with Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro
 Apple is finally tackling the challenge of ‘ergonomically terrible’ touchscreen laptops.
 by Terrence O'Brien Close Terrence O'Brien Weekend Editor Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.
 Follow Follow See All by Terrence O'Brien 
 and Antonio G. Di Benedetto Close Antonio G. Di Benedetto Reviewer, Laptops Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.
 Follow Follow See All by Antonio G. Di Benedetto 
 Oct 28, 2026, 5:16 PM UTC Link 
 Share 
 Gift 
 The difference in thickness is small compared to the non-touch MacBook Pro models. Part Of All the news from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event see all updates Steve Jobs famously called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible,” and for over a decade, Apple stridently refused to make one. Today that all changes with the MacBook Pro — the company’s first laptop to embrace a touch interface. While it’s unlikely that Apple can fix all the “terrible” ergonomics of having to lift your arm up and touch a laptop screen, the company has put some effort into making macOS more touch-friendly.
 The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display weighs just 3 pounds, which is noticeably lighter than the current generation of non-touch MacBook Pros, which start at 3.4 pounds for the newly introduced M6 models . The difference is even bigger when you jump to the 16-inch model, which clocks in at 4 pounds, while the M5 Pro version without a touchscreen is 4.7.
 Previous Next 
 1 / 3 The screen is incredibly bright and saturated. Also exciting is the return of the glowing Apple logo. It’s a seemingly minor feature, but one that definitely got the audience excited during the introduction, and marks the return of a bit of flair to the MacBook lineup which, let’s be fair, has grown a bit utilitarian-looking over the years.
 Unsurprisingly, there is a price premium for the new MacBook Pro PROLED XDR. The touchscreen OLED model starts at $2,899, $400 more than the otherwise similarly-specced M5 Pro MacBook Pro.
